llm.summary: This skill is mainly a routing/onboarding helper, but it also automatically runs local scripts, checks GitHub, scans installed skills, and writes local state without a separate user confirmation.

dimensions.detail: The scripts inspect local skill installation directories, print real source paths, fetch remote SKILL.md files from GitHub for version comparison, and create a stamp file under the user's home directory.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer backdoor or automatic update execution was found; however, the update notice recommends an unpinned npx-based reinstall command for the whole AI KEY set.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill has broad natural-language triggers and says the version-check script should run every time it is invoked, even when the check is silent, which can cause environment access during casual activation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package writes a 24-hour update-check timestamp under ~/.aikey and shared family guidance includes automatic memory/vault writes under some conditions; no privilege escalation, credential access, or destructive behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The router purpose is coherent, but the skill adds automatic version checking and local skill discovery that are broader than simply selecting a downstream AI KEY skill and generating a prompt.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing if you do not want a skill to run local bash scripts automatically. This package is not destructive, but it can check GitHub once per day, enumerate installed AI KEY skills and their real paths, and write local timestamp or memory files. Prefer an opt-in/no-script version if you only need a static router.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The scanner's concern is partly supported: local discovery is relevant to routing, but the automatic GitHub update check and home-directory stamp are maintenance behavior beyond the advertised front-desk router role.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Supported: SKILL.md instructs running scripts on invocation; new-version.sh performs network checks and writes a stamp, while list-skills.sh enumerates installed skills.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Supported as a review concern: shell execution is disclosed, but it is not tightly user-controlled and is broader than text-only routing.
[AE1] expected: Downgraded: the package's direct references were present and inspected; the instruction to read a selected downstream skill is normal routing behavior, though those downstream artifacts are outside this package.
[TM1] expected: Downgraded: the rm usage only removes a temporary failed remote fetch file inside a mktemp directory and does not indicate destructive behavior.
[LP3] unexpected: Supported as a scoping concern because the skill relies on shell scripts but does not provide a separate permission boundary or opt-in for those commands.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger phrases are intentional onboarding behavior, but they compound the script-execution concern because activation can cause local and network checks.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Supported: SKILL.md says the tool is a triage desk, while later sections add automatic scripts, local inventory discovery, and update checking.
[SQP-3] expected: Language and citation-style constraints appear to be product/content guidance for a Chinese-oriented skill, not evidence of malicious behavior; the skill also says to follow the user's language.
[RP1] expected: Downgraded: the npx command is printed as manual update guidance and is not executed by the skill, but users should still treat it as an unpinned install command.
